title: A Loan From the Future: What a National Park Really Protects
title_zh: 一笔来自未来的贷款：国家公园真正保护的是什么
intro_zh: 本文约 516 词，共 8 段，围绕国家公园的三重意义（保护物种、服务公众、调节旅游压力）展开，含黄石公园、中国首批国家公园与非洲社区旅游等具体事例与数据，重点词约 6 个。

paragraphs.en: In 1872, the United States did something no country had done before. It set aside two million acres of land in Wyoming and Montana and declared that the area belonged to no private owner. Yellowstone became the world's first national park. The law said the land was kept for the benefit of the people. That short sentence started a new idea: some places are too valuable to be sold.
paragraphs.zh: 1872 年，美国做了一件此前没有任何国家做过的事。它在怀俄明州和蒙大拿州划出两百万英亩土地，宣布这片区域不属于任何私人所有者。黄石由此成为世界上第一座国家公园。法律规定，这片土地是为了人民的益处而保留的。这短短一句话开启了一个新观念：有些地方太珍贵，不能拿来出售。

paragraphs.en: Today more than 6,000 national parks exist around the world, from the mountains of Nepal to the beaches of Costa Rica. Together they shelter a large share of the world's plant and animal species. China joined the movement in 2021, when it named its first five national parks, including Sanjiangyuan on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. They cover about 230,000 square kilometres, an area larger than many countries.
paragraphs.zh: 如今全世界有六千多座国家公园，从尼泊尔的高山到哥斯达黎加的海滩。它们共同庇护着世界上相当大一部分动植物物种。中国于 2021 年加入这一行列，公布首批五个国家公园，其中包括位于青藏高原的三江源。它们覆盖约二十三万平方公里，比许多国家还要大。

paragraphs.en: The first job of a national park is to protect life. A park is not just scenery; it is a reserve where animals can live without being hunted out or pushed away. In Yellowstone, wolves disappeared in the 1920s. Without them, deer stayed near the rivers and ate the young trees. When wolves were brought back in 1995, the whole valley slowly changed: trees grew again, birds returned, and even the rivers ran straighter.
paragraphs.zh: 国家公园的第一项职责是保护生命。公园不只是风景，它是一个保护区，动物在这里可以生活，不会被猎杀殆尽，也不会被驱赶出去。在黄石，狼在二十世纪二十年代消失了。没有狼，鹿便停留在河边，啃食小树。1995 年狼被重新引入后，整个山谷慢慢发生了变化：树木重新生长，鸟儿回来了，连河道都变得更直了。

paragraphs.en: The second job is easier to see. A national park gives ordinary people a place to go. In many countries the most beautiful land once belonged only to the rich. National parks changed that. A factory worker and a professor can stand at the same viewpoint, breathe the same air and pay the same ticket price. This was a quiet revolution in who owns beauty.
paragraphs.zh: 第二项职责更容易看见。国家公园给普通人一个可去的地方。在许多国家，最美的土地曾经只属于富人。国家公园改变了这一点。一名工厂工人和一位教授可以站在同一个观景点，呼吸同样的空气，付同样的门票钱。这是一场关于“美属于谁”的静悄悄的革命。

paragraphs.en: Doctors now take this seriously. Studies in several countries have found that people who spend about two hours a week in green spaces report better health and less stress. A national park is the largest green space many city families can reach. For children who grow up among screens and traffic, it may be the only place where they hear real silence. Some parks even run free bus days for schoolchildren.
paragraphs.zh: 医生们如今也认真看待这件事。若干国家的研究发现，每周在绿色空间中待上大约两小时的人，自述健康状况更好、压力更小。对许多城市家庭来说，国家公园是他们能到达的最大一片绿。对于在屏幕与车流中长大的孩子，这也许是他们唯一能听见真正安静的地方。一些公园还为学童开设免费巴士日。

paragraphs.en: But popularity brings pressure. Yellowstone receives about 4.5 million visitors a year, and in summer its roads can look like a city street. Rubbish, noise and illegal camping damage the very things people come to see. Rangers say the biggest problem is not the number of visitors but the way they behave. Simple things help: shuttle buses, timed tickets and clear signs.
paragraphs.zh: 但受欢迎也带来压力。黄石每年接待约四百五十万游客，夏天园内的道路看起来就像城市街道。垃圾、噪音和违规露营，破坏的恰恰是人们前来看的东西。巡护员说，最大的问题不是游客数量，而是他们的行为方式。一些简单的办法有帮助：接驳巴士、分时门票和清晰的标识。

paragraphs.en: Money matters too. In some African countries, tourism is now the main income of villages near the parks. A lion that is alive earns more than a lion that is shot, and that simple fact saves thousands of animals every year. Still, every park must find a balance: too many rules and people stop coming; too few and the place is ruined.
paragraphs.zh: 钱也很重要。在一些非洲国家，旅游业如今是公园周边村庄的主要收入来源。一头活着的狮子比一头被射杀的狮子更赚钱，而这个简单的事实每年救下成千上万只动物。不过，每座公园都必须找到平衡：规矩太多，人们就不来了；规矩太少，这个地方就毁了。

paragraphs.en: A national park is often called a gift from the past. It is better described as a loan from the future. The people who created Yellowstone could not imagine 4.5 million visitors, but they understood one simple thing: some land should never be sold, because it belongs to everyone, including those not yet born.
paragraphs.zh: 人们常说国家公园是来自过去的礼物。更准确的说法是，它是一笔来自未来的贷款。创建黄石的人无法想象四百五十万游客，但他们懂得一件简单的事：有些土地永远不该被出售，因为它属于每一个人，包括那些尚未出生的人。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Yellowstone was built and managed in its early years.
Why national parks matter and what they have to balance.
How tourism earns money for villages in African countries.
Why city children need more green spaces near their homes.
questions.explain: 全文先讲国家公园的起源（黄石），再讲三重意义：保护物种、服务公众健康、带动当地收入，最后落到“平衡”与“向未来借来的土地”，所以 B 最全面。A 只覆盖第一段，C 只覆盖第七段，D 只覆盖第五段。

questions.q: According to the passage, what happened in Yellowstone after wolves were brought back in 1995?
options: Deer numbers rose quickly along the rivers.
The park was closed to visitors for several years.
Trees grew again and even the rivers changed.
Rangers began to feed deer in the valley.
questions.explain: 第三段明确写道：狼回归后树木重新生长、鸟儿回来、连河道都变得更直，故选 C。文中说没有狼时鹿啃食小树，并非鹿数量激增，A 错；B、D 文中均未提及。

questions.q: What can be inferred about tourism near some African national parks?
options: It has become the only job for local people.
It gives local people a reason to keep wild animals alive.
It has made lions more dangerous than before.
It brings very little money to the villages.
questions.explain: 第七段说“一头活着的狮子比一头被射杀的狮子更赚钱”，因而每年救下大量动物，可推知旅游让当地人有了保护野生动物的经济动机，B 正确。文中只说 tourism 是主要收入之一，并未说是唯一职业，A 过度推断；C、D 与原文相反或无依据。

questions.q: The phrase 'a loan from the future' in the last paragraph suggests that a national park is ______.
options: something taken from nature and never given back
money that future generations will have to pay back
something we hold for a time and must pass on
a place that will finally be sold to private owners
questions.explain: 把国家公园比作“来自未来的贷款”，意思是它不属于我们这一代人，我们只是暂时保管，必须完好地传给后代，C 最贴切。A 与“属于每个人”矛盾；B 把比喻误解为金钱债务；D 与全文“永不售卖”的观点相反。
